summary: Review A (correctness) of Phase 1 at audited head 8ec0f873c. The affected-app logic is correct against FR-1, D4, and C1 to C10. The 48-case suite passes 48/48 (exit 0). Git handling, lockfile matching (fix c03e201ea), global inputs (D4), workspace globs, and exit codes are correct. The six real ranges of task 1.4 check out, including the acorn explanation for the extra www id of c0e2cfbb1. Scope is clean. Two Minor non-blocking findings.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Minor] scripts/ci/__tests__/helpers/scratch.mjs:112: The fixture TABLE_ROWS sets marketing tag to "c${BUILD_ID:0:8}", but the real scripts/ci/apps.json sets "c$${build_id%%-*}" (the bash derivation of M19). Rationale: the strategy P1.2 says the fixture writes the 10 rows of spec section 2a, so the fixture diverges from the real table. No P1 test reads the fixture tag text: the script reads only id and path, and B-21 reads the real table and checks presence, not text. Zero P1 impact. P2 AC-2.3 re-checks the real table. Risk: a future P1 test that relies on the fixture tag would diverge from the real table.

F2 [Minor] scripts/ci/affected-apps.mjs:685 vs scripts/ci/__tests__/affected-apps.test.mjs:298: The script matches a catalog spec with String(spec).startsWith("catalog:"), but the test helper catalogRows matches all[name] === "catalog:". Rationale: no current manifest uses a ranged catalog spec (catalog:^x.y.z), so the expected set and the script output coincide and B-18 passes. If a future track adds a ranged catalog spec, catalogRows under-counts the expected set and B-18 fails spuriously even though the script is right. Latent fragility, not a current defect.

Detectors pass at HEAD: built-ins detector exit 1; require(/import( detector exit 1; no-shell detector exit 1; hash detector exit 1; node --check exit 0 on the script and both test files; JSDoc detector exit 1; A9 detector exit 1; git diff --stat f302b4edc..HEAD -- scripts/ci/__tests__ prints nothing.

Architecture guardrail (strategy 1.5): no app, package, test, or workflow imports scripts/ci/affected-apps.mjs as a module. git grep for 'affected-apps' (excluding measure/) hits only the script itself, the test file, and the harness helper, which spawns it via node (spawnSync of process.execPath), not import. No build-graph run was needed: the script is standalone ESM with no exported symbols consumed elsewhere; the contract is the CLI plus one JSON line on stdout. Used git grep for callers per the heavy-run rule for build-graph.
